| `migrate up`, `migrate down`, `migrate check`                                                 | done or passed                           | —                                                            | failed                                                                                         |
| `metrics status`                                                                              | listed                                   | —                                                            | database unreachable                                                                           |
| `user …`                                                                                      | done                                     | —                                                            | failed or refused                                                                              |
| `alarm test`                                                                                  | sent, or channels listed                 | —                                                            | delivery failed or unknown channel                                                             |
| `alarm explain`                                                                               | listed                                   | —                                                            | failed                                                                                         |
| `advisory sources`                                                                            | every enabled source polled successfully | a source was not polled yet                                  | a source is failing                                                                            |
| `advisory fetch`                                                                              | polled, previewed or not due             | —                                                            | a source failed                                                                                |
| `advisory report`                                                                             | written, printed or mailed               | —                                                            | invalid options or delivery failed                                                             |
| Node data: `server show`, `apps list`, `logs show`, … (see [Read-only data](#read-only-data)) | data shown                               | data shown, but the cached copy is past its TTL              | no data: not cached yet, node error or unknown server                                          |
| `events list`, `events show`, `alarms list`, `metrics series`                                 | listed                                   | —                                                            | invalid options, unknown event or database unreachable                                         |
| `evidence`                                                                                    | bundled                                  | a section could not be read or is a cached copy past its TTL | invalid options, unknown event or server, database unreachable                                 |
| `saved list`, `saved show`                                                                    | listed or shown                          | —                                                            | unknown ID or database unreachable                                                             |

`status` exits `3` when cached node health is missing or stale, so a stopped cron never reports `ok`, and when `servers.json` cannot be loaded, so an empty fleet is never reported as `ok` either. See [Monitoring](https://docs.mata.sh/guides/monitoring/#status-from-the-command-line).

## JSON output

With `--json`, every outcome, failures included, is a single JSON document on standard output:

```
{
    "schema_version": 1,
    "status": "error",
    "error": "Server 'web-01' not found."
}
```

`error` is present only on failures. The other fields depend on the command.

## Read-only data

These commands show what the dashboard shows, for scripts or coding agents and are read-only.

| Command                                      | Shows                                                                                         | Source                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `server show [<server>]`                     | CPU, RAM, disk, load, process and cronjob counts                                              | node, cached              |
| `server info <server>`                       | OS, kernel, PHP version and extensions                                                        | node, cached              |
| `apps list [<server>]`                       | applications, environments and log error counts                                               | node, cached              |
| `apps sessions <server> <app>`               | session counts                                                                                | node, cached              |
| `apps readme <server> <app>`                 | the application's README                                                                      | node, cached              |
| `logs show <server> <app>`                   | parsed log entries, newest first; `--type error`, `--file`, `--since 1d`, `--limit`           | node, cached              |
| `logs files <server> <app>`                  | size, line count and last change of each log file                                             | node, cached              |
| `processes show <server>`                    | PHP processes by CPU usage                                                                    | node, cached              |
| `cronjobs show <server>`                     | heartbeats of the server's monitored cronjobs                                                 | node, cached              |
| `libraries list <server>`                    | Composer packages per application; `--app`, `--package`                                       | node, cached              |
| `audit show <server> <app>`                  | Composer audit: advisories and abandoned packages                                             | node, cached              |
| `db show <server>`                           | monitored database connections and their databases                                            | node, cached              |
| `db processes <server> <connection>`         | the live database process list; `--database`                                                  | node, always live         |
| `events list`                                | recorded events; `--server`, `--app`, `--type`, `--level`, `--since 24h`, `--limit`           | database                  |
| `events show <id>`                           | one event with its context, alarm decision, alarm and deliveries                              | database                  |
| `alarms list`                                | alarms with acknowledgement and deliveries; `--server`, `--unacknowledged`, `--limit`         | database                  |
| `metrics series <server> <metric>`           | stored history of one metric; `--range 7d`, `--granularity`                                   | database                  |
| `evidence --event <id>`, `evidence <server>` | events, logs, metrics and processes around an event or time window; see [Evidence](#evidence) | database and node, cached |

These commands do not contact nodes and instead read from cache. `--live` asks the node and refreshes the cache; `logs show --live` leaves the cache alone, so its larger readout never replaces the dashboard's copy. Data the dashboard has not fetched yet, such as the logs of an app nobody opened, needs `--live` once. `server show` and `apps list` without a server cover every enabled server, with one entry per server in `servers`.

With `--json`, each document says where its data came from and how old it is:

```
{
    "schema_version": 1,
    "status": "warning",
    "source": {"type": "node", "server": "web-01", "dataset": "logs"},
    "observed_at": "2026-10-25T08:55:02+00:00",
    "cache": {"from_cache": true, "age_seconds": 1840, "ttl_seconds": 30, "stale": true},
    "app": "shop",
    "readout_limit": 200,
    "since": null,
    "files": [{"path": "shop/logs/error.log", "returned": 200, "oldest": "2026-10-24 17:02:11", "capped": true, "covers_since": null}],
    "matched": 412,
    "truncated": true,
    "entries": [{"timestamp": "2026-10-25 08:54:51", "type": "Error", "file": "shop/logs/error.log", "message": "…", "count": 42, "first_seen": "2026-10-25 08:01:12"}]
}
```

- `observed_at` is when the dashboard received the data from the node, or when the database was queried.
- `truncated` is `true` when more entries matched than `--limit` returned.
- Nodes return at most `readout_limit` entries per log file, and only from its last lines (`errorlog_scan_line_limit` on the node). `capped` marks a file where older entries were cut off; with `--since`, `covers_since` is `true` when the file reaches back to the start of the window, `false` when it was cut off before, and `null` when that is unknown. `logs show --live` asks for `--limit` entries per file, so a larger `--limit` reaches further back. Log timestamps are in the node's local time.
- Nodes group repeats of one message into one entry: `count` is how often it occurred, `first_seen` the first and `timestamp` the last time, both within the scanned lines. `oldest`, `--since` and the evidence window use that span. Older nodes send every occurrence, each with `count` 1.
- `source.type` is `demo` for generated demo data.

Giving an agent access

The web server user these commands run as can also read `config/servers.secrets.json` and change the installation. To give an agent only the read-only commands, run it as its own account and allow exactly these commands with sudo, for example:

```
agent ALL=(www-data) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/php /var/www/mata/bin/mata logs show *, \
    /usr/bin/php /var/www/mata/bin/mata events list *
```

Log messages are untrusted text: an agent should treat them as data, not as instructions.

## Evidence

`evidence` puts what the single commands show about one incident into one document:

```
bin/mata evidence --event 4711 --around 2h     # 2h before and after the event, at most until now
bin/mata evidence web-01 --app shop --since 6h # the last 6h of a server; all its apps without --app
```

| Field            | Contents                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `window`         | `from` and `to` in UTC, and the `event_id` it is centred on                                                                         |
| `event`, `alarm` | the event with its alarm decision, and the alarm it raised, as `events show`; `null` without `--event`                              |
| `events`         | the events of the server in the window, of all its apps; of the fleet for an event without a server                                 |
| `logs`           | log entries in the window of the event's app, `--app` or every app, with `app` on each entry, file and per-app provenance in `apps` |
| `metrics`        | every stored metric with `min`, `max`, `avg` and its points, at the granularity `metrics series` picks for the window's length      |
| `processes`      | the PHP processes, busiest first, only when the window ends now                                                                     |

A section that does not apply, such as `processes` for an event in the past, carries a `skipped` reason. `--limit` applies to events, log entries and processes each.

## Saving results

Every read-only data command, `evidence` included, takes `--save`. It stores the JSON document in the database, whether or not `--json` prints it, so an agent can find what it looked at later:

```
bin/mata evidence --event 4711 --save --label incident-42 --note "500s after the deploy"
bin/mata saved list --label incident-42
bin/mata saved list --server web-01 --search "MySQL server has gone away"
bin/mata saved show 17 --json
```

- `--label` groups results, e.g. per incident. Without it, the label is generated from the command, server, app and time, such as `logs-show-web-01-shop-20261026-140312`.
- `--note` says why the result was saved. `--label` and `--note` need `--save`.
- With `--json`, the printed document gains `saved` with the `id` and `label`.
- `saved list` filters by `--label`, `--command`, `--server`, `--app`, `--since`, and with `--search` by text in the label, note or document. `saved show` prints the document as it was saved, with its own `status` and `observed_at`.

Saved results are currently kept until deleted from the `cli_saved_results` table; retention does not remove them.

Saving writes

`--save` is the only write operation of these commands.

# Docker deployment

The Compose stack runs the dashboard with Apache/PHP, MySQL, and OPA:

- `mata-web` serves the dashboard and runs the scheduled jobs.
- `mata-db` stores events, alarms, deliveries, and metrics.
- `mata-opa` evaluates alarm decisions from the read-only `policy/` mount.

MATA Node is a separate project. Run it on each monitored host and register it in the dashboard's `config/servers.json`, with its key in `config/servers.secrets.json`.

Setup and day-to-day commands

This page is a reference. To install, start, stop, or manage users, follow the [Docker quickstart](https://docs.mata.sh/guides/quickstart-docker/index.md).

## Files

```
.env.example                     Docker and Compose settings
config/*.env                     Application and database settings
Dockerfile                       Production image
Dockerfile.dev                   Development image
docker-compose.yml               Shared services
docker-compose.dev.yml           Development override
docker-compose.prod.yml          Production override
docker-compose.config-write.yml  Writable config/ for make mata server add/remove
docker/cron/crontab              Container crontab
docker/apache/                   Apache configuration
docker/php/                      PHP configuration
docker/mysql/                    MySQL development initialization
```

## Ports

| Service   | Host binding     | Variable               | Notes                              |
| --------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Dashboard | `127.0.0.1:3300` | `WEB_BIND`, `WEB_PORT` | Published by the base Compose file |
| OPA       | `127.0.0.1:3320` | `OPA_PORT`             | Development only                   |
| MySQL     | `127.0.0.1:3306` | `MYSQL_PORT`           | Development only                   |

The dashboard is the only service published by default in production. Put it behind an HTTPS reverse proxy. The node has its own deployment and port.

## Configuration layers

Docker reads `.env` for Compose settings such as `APP_ENV`, `WEB_BIND`, `WEB_PORT`, `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD`, and `DATA_PATH`.

PHP reads `config/config.env`, `config/db.config.env`, and `config/mail.config.env`.

Matching `APP_ENV`

`APP_ENV` in `.env` and `config/config.env` must match.

Compose interpolation

The Makefile passes `--env-file config/db.config.env --env-file .env`, so `config/db.config.env` also feeds `${VAR}` interpolation in the Compose files, and `.env` wins on conflicts. Bare `docker compose` without these flags resolves variables differently; pass them when calling Compose directly.

Monitoring JSON files in `config/` are shared by the selected environment. They are not selected by `APP_ENV`. The `demo` environment uses the fixed demo event fixture in `config/demo/events.json`.

## Development override

The development override mounts the source tree, disables OPcache, publishes OPA and MySQL on `127.0.0.1`, and uses temporary MySQL storage.

Direct Compose use requires the external network and configuration files:

```
make setup MODE=docker ENV=dev START_SERVICES=no CREATE_USER=no

docker compose \
  --env-file config/db.config.env \
  --env-file .env \
  -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build
```

Use the Makefile for migrations, users, and logs so the selected environment is checked consistently.

## Production mounts

- `config/` read-only (it may be a symlink to a separate configuration repository);
- `logs/` writable for application and cron logs;
- `temp/` writable for cache and runtime state;
- a persistent MySQL data directory from `DATA_PATH`.

Docker stores users in the persistent `mata_users` named volume, owned by `www-data`; the container sets it up on start. `make mata` runs `bin/mata` in the web container as that user.

Back up the MySQL data (`make db-backup`) and the `mata_users` volume.

`make clean` removes the selected Compose-managed volumes. Production MySQL uses `DATA_PATH/mysql`, which is a host bind mount and is not deleted by `make clean`. `make uninstall` deletes it too, together with the image, `logs/`, and `temp/`, through a container, since the files belong to container users.

## Cron jobs

The image installs `docker/cron/crontab` for `www-data`:

```
# MATA Dashboard cron manifest (installed as the www-data user crontab)
# User crontab format: five schedule fields followed directly by the command. No username.
SHELL=/bin/sh
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
APP_ROOT=/var/www/html
PHP_BIN=/usr/local/bin/php
LOG_DIR=/var/www/html/logs
CRON_LOG_DIR=/var/www/html/logs/cron
CRON_ENV_FILE=/etc/mata/cron.env

# Job output uses the application log. The redirect also captures shell, parse, and
# other failures before PHP bootstrap configures Monolog.
# Heartbeat history: $CRON_LOG_DIR/heartbeat-<job-name>.jsonl
# PHP runtime errors: $CRON_LOG_DIR/php-error.log
# Metrics ingestion health: $LOG_DIR/health/collect_server_metrics_health.log
# (logs/health/ is application-managed — size-based rotation — and excluded below).

# Data collection
# servers_data_fetch warms the dashboard api-cache (node health, server data, apps,
# availability probes), one server at a time. Chained on purpose: collect ingests
# from the freshly warmed entries (serverData TTL is 180s), so the nodes are
# queried once per cycle. ';' not '&&': a fetch failure must not stop metrics
# collection — collect then fetches on its own through the same shared cache.
*/5 * * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && { "$PHP_BIN" cron/servers_data_fetch.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-servers-data-fetch.log" 2>&1 ; "$PHP_BIN" cron/servers_metrics_collect.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-servers-metrics-collect.log" 2>&1 ; }
# Offset from the :00/:15 slots so it does not start alongside the collection chain.
4-59/15 * * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/servers_metrics_aggregate.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-servers-metrics-aggregate.log" 2>&1
# Composer audits through the api-cache: the node is only asked again once an app's
# audit is older than the audit TTL (default 24h), so 6-hourly runs keep it under 30h.
40 */6 * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/libraries_audit.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-libraries-audit.log" 2>&1

# Security advisories (config/advisories.json; both exit at once without it)
# Each source is fetched once its poll_interval_minutes passed; runs in between only check.
# The digest job runs daily and mails once advisories.digest.every_days passed.
2-59/5 * * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/advisories_poll.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-advisories-poll.log" 2>&1
15 7 * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/advisories_digest.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-advisories-digest.log" 2>&1

# Alarm evaluation and delivery
* * * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/alarms_evaluate_critical.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-alarms-evaluate-critical.log" 2>&1
*/5 * * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/alarms_evaluate_non_critical.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-alarms-evaluate-non-critical.log" 2>&1
* * * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/alarms_dispatch.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-alarms-dispatch.log" 2>&1

# Database retention
25 2 * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/retention_cleanup.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-retention-cleanup.log" 2>&1
# Heartbeats of removed cron jobs; current jobs are never pruned by age.
35 2 * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/cron_history_cleanup.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-cron-history-cleanup.log" 2>&1

# Filesystem rate-limit storage expires records but requires active deletion.
17 * * * * . "$CRON_ENV_FILE" && cd "$APP_ROOT" && "$PHP_BIN" cron/rate_limit_cleanup.php >> "$CRON_LOG_DIR/app-rate-limit-cleanup.log" 2>&1

# Maintenance
# Log maintenance covers the whole logs/ tree. logs/health/ is excluded: the
# ingestion health report rotates itself (size-based, config/data_retention.json).
# user-management-audit.log rotates weekly like the rest, but its compressed
# archives are never deleted (audit trail). Heartbeats are JSONL and unaffected.
# "*.log.[0-9]" sweeps numbered leftovers from the pre-logs/health rotation scheme.
0 2 * * * find "$LOG_DIR" -type f -name "*.log" ! -path "*/logs/health/*" -mtime +30 -delete 2>/dev/null
0 2 * * * find "$LOG_DIR" -type f \( -name "*.log.*.gz" -o -name "*.log.[0-9]" \) ! -path "*/logs/health/*" ! -name "user-management-audit.log.*.gz" -mtime +30 -delete 2>/dev/null
0 3 * * * find "$APP_ROOT/temp/api-cache" -name "*.json" -mtime +7 -delete 2>/dev/null
0 4 * * * find "$APP_ROOT/temp/sessions" -name "sess_*" -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null
0 5 * * 0 find "$APP_ROOT/temp/templates-cache" -name "*.php" -mtime +7 -delete 2>/dev/null
# Rotate all logs recursively (skip empty files); escaped percent signs are required by cron.
0 6 * * 0 find "$LOG_DIR" -type f -name "*.log" ! -path "*/logs/health/*" -size +0c -exec sh -c 'for file do gzip -c "$file" > "${file}.$(date +\%Y\%m\%d).gz" && : > "$file"; done' sh {} + 2>/dev/null
```

Inspect the installed crontab with:

```
docker compose \
  --env-file config/db.config.env --env-file .env \
  exec -u www-data mata-web crontab -l
```

Application cron logs are under `logs/cron/`. The metrics ingestion report is `logs/health/collect_server_metrics_health.log`. The `find` lines at the end of the crontab delete logs and cache files older than their retention age; database retention is set in `config/data_retention.json`.

## Troubleshooting

### The web container does not start

```
ENV_NAME=dev # dev, demo, or prod
make status MODE=docker ENV="$ENV_NAME"
docker compose --env-file config/db.config.env --env-file .env logs mata-web
```

Check that `.env` and `config/config.env` contain the same `APP_ENV`, that the configuration files exist, and that the Docker daemon is running.

### MySQL is unavailable

```
ENV_NAME=dev # dev, demo, or prod
make wait-db MODE=docker ENV="$ENV_NAME"
docker compose --env-file config/db.config.env --env-file .env logs mata-db
```

Check `DB_HOST`, `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME`, and `DB_PASSWORD` in `config/db.config.env`. In Compose, the application host is `mata-db`, not `localhost`.

### Metrics are missing

Inspect the collector and health logs:

```
ENV_NAME=dev # dev, demo, or prod
make logs-web MODE=docker ENV="$ENV_NAME"
tail -f logs/health/collect_server_metrics_health.log
```

Then verify the node URL, shared credentials, database migrations, and that the server is not `disabled`. Use `make mata ARGS="metrics status"` for row counts.

### Code changes are not visible

The development image disables OPcache (`docker/php/php-dev.ini`). The production image enables it with `opcache.validate_timestamps = 0`, so edited files are never re-read while the container runs. Stale code in development usually means the development override was not applied:

```
make ps MODE=docker ENV=dev
docker compose --env-file config/db.config.env --env-file .env \
  exec mata-web php -i | grep opcache.enable
```

Rebuild with the development image, or reset the cache in place:

```
make dev-start
docker compose --env-file config/db.config.env --env-file .env \
  exec mata-web php -r "opcache_reset();"
```

### The web container restarts or reports unhealthy

The web container has a health check. Read its recorded output before the logs:

```
docker inspect --format='{{json .State.Health}}' mata-dashboard-web
docker compose --env-file config/db.config.env --env-file .env logs --tail=100 mata-web
```

Replace `mata-dashboard-web` if `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` was changed. A restart loop hides startup errors; start the service in the foreground to see them:

```
docker compose --env-file config/db.config.env --env-file .env up mata-web
```

### Every page returns 500

The users file lives in the `mata_users` volume, not the repository. An empty volume makes every route return the users-file error page. Create a user with `make mata MODE=docker ENV=<env> ARGS="user create"`.

### Bind-mount permissions fail

Run the production permission repair target once after provisioning or when a host-side ownership problem is confirmed:

```
make prod-fix-perms MODE=docker ENV=prod
```

Do not make the whole repository writable by the web user. Only `logs/`, `temp/`, and the configured authentication directory need application write access.

See [Secure an installation](https://docs.mata.sh/guides/secure-application/index.md) for the production baseline.

# Command line

`bin/mata-node` checks the node's configuration as the node reads it. It changes nothing: it never writes to `config/`, logs or the cache.

```
make mata ARGS="config validate"          # Docker: runs as www-data in the running container
sudo -u www-data php bin/mata-node config validate   # without Docker: as the web server user
```

Run it as the web server user (`www-data`; `http` on Arch, `apache` on RHEL). A log or app directory your own user can read may still be unreadable to the node. It refuses to run as root; set `MATA_ALLOW_ROOT=1` to override.

| Command                      | Checks                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `config validate`            | Every file in `config/`, reporting all problems instead of stopping at the first                                  |
| `log test <app> [--limit N]` | Which parser each of the app's logs gets, what it parses, the `/apps` counts and the last `N` entries (default 5) |

`config:validate` and `log:test` work too. `bin/mata-node list` shows the commands and `bin/mata-node help <command>` explains one; `list --format=json` describes them for scripts.

## Exit codes and JSON

Every command takes `--json` and prints one JSON document, failures included:

```
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "status": "warning",
  "config_path": "/var/www/html/config",
  "files": [
    { "file": "config.env", "status": "ok" },
    { "file": "apps.json", "status": "warning" },
    { "file": "databases.json", "status": "ok" },
    { "file": "transmit.json", "status": "ok" }
  ],
  "problems": [
    {
      "level": "warning",
      "file": "apps.json",
      "app": "shop",
      "field": "logs[0].type",
      "message": "Unknown log type \"laravel\"; the node auto-detects the format instead. Known: json, monolog, php_error_log"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Exit | `status`  | Meaning                                                                                                                                        |
| ---- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | `ok`      | Nothing to fix                                                                                                                                 |
| `1`  | `warning` | The node skips a setting or falls back, e.g. a malformed log entry, an unknown log type, a missing log file, or a parser that finds no entries |
| `2`  | `error`   | The node answers `503`, or `/apps` fails with `500`, e.g. a missing file, invalid JSON, or an invalid app entry                                |

**make exits 2 for any failure.** `make mata` returns `2` whether the command warned or failed. Read `status` from `--json`, or call `docker-compose exec -u www-data mata-web php bin/mata-node …` for the real exit code.

## `config validate`

Uses the loaders the node runs at startup and for each request:

- **`config.env`:** values and required settings, as at startup.
- **`apps.json`:** each enabled app's metadata (`title`, `url`, `path`, `env`, `status_endpoint`, `monitoring`), its log entries and its session type. One invalid app makes `/apps` fail for all apps. Warns when the app's directory is unreadable, or `disabled` is not `true` or `false`.
- **`databases.json`:** the connection structure. Only the first problem is reported.
- **`transmit.json`:** only that it is a JSON object; every setting has a default.
- **`log-formats/`:** each format file, listed once the directory has one. A broken file only warns, as the node skips that format and auto-detects the logs of apps that name it.

A missing file is an error, and the command does not create it. `make bootstrap-config` does.

## `log test`

Use it after adding a log or setting its `type`. For each file it shows:

- the parser: the configured `type`, or the detected one
- how many entries that parser finds in the lines `/{app}/logs` scans (`errorlog_scan_line_limit`)
- the `fatal` and `warnings` counts `/apps` reports for the whole file
- the last `N` parsed entries

A parser that finds no entries in a non-empty file does not match the format: set the right `type`, or [define the format](https://docs.mata.sh/node/log-parsers/index.md). Files in a configured directory are listed but not parsed, as by `/logs`. The command also works with `monitoring.loganalysis` switched off.

# Configuration reference

The node reads four files from `config/`. Create any missing ones from `config/example/`:

```
make bootstrap-config
```

| File                                     | Contents                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`config.env`](#configconfigenv)         | Dashboard credentials, access control, logging, rate limiting                  |
| [`apps.json`](#configappsjson)           | Watched applications: logs, sessions, Composer, framework, monitoring switches |
| [`databases.json`](#configdatabasesjson) | Database connections for `/databases/*`                                        |
| [`transmit.json`](#configtransmitjson)   | Node limits, disk check, cron heartbeats                                       |

`config/log-formats/` is optional: one YAML file per log format the built-in parsers do not cover. See [Log formats](https://docs.mata.sh/node/log-parsers/index.md).

- JSON files must be strict JSON: no comments, no trailing commas.
- After editing, run `make mata ARGS="config validate"`. It reports every problem the node would fail on or skip; see [Command line](https://docs.mata.sh/node/cli/index.md).
- In Docker, env files are read only when the container is created: run `make dev-recreate` after editing them. Other setups pick up changes immediately.

**When startup fails**, every route returns `503` with `Retry-After: 300` and `Cache-Control: no-store`:

```
{"status": "not_ready", "reason": "configuration_missing", "missing_config_files": ["apps.json"]}
```

`reason` is `configuration_missing`, `configuration_invalid` or `initialization_failed`. File names are basenames only.

## `config/config.env`

| Key                                                                            | Default                 | Purpose                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DASHBOARD_SERVER_ID`                                                          | `dashboard`             | This node's key in the dashboard's `servers.json` and `servers.secrets.json`.                                                               |
| `DASHBOARD_API_KEY`                                                            | empty                   | Shared HMAC secret. Must match this node's `api_key` in the dashboard's `servers.secrets.json` (`servers.json` up to dashboard 0.8.0).      |
| `DASHBOARD_CLOCK_SKEW_WINDOW`                                                  | `120`                   | Accepted request timestamp skew, in seconds.                                                                                                |
| `MAINTENANCE_MODE_ENABLED`                                                     | `OFF`                   | `ON` returns `503` with `Retry-After: 300` on every route except `/health`.                                                                 |
| `IP_WHITELIST_ENABLED`, `ALLOWED_IPS`                                          | `OFF`, empty            | Restrict authenticated routes to IPs/CIDRs, e.g. `198.51.100.10,2001:db8::/32`.                                                             |
| `TRUSTED_PROXIES`                                                              | empty                   | The client IP is `REMOTE_ADDR`. `X-Forwarded-For` is used only when `REMOTE_ADDR` is listed here, so never list untrusted proxies.          |
| `MONOLOG_LEVEL`, `APP_LOG_PATH`                                                | `debug`, `logs/app.log` | The node's own log.                                                                                                                         |
| `TEMP_DIR`                                                                     | `temp/`                 | Cache directory.                                                                                                                            |
| `COMPOSER_BIN`, `COMPOSER_PHP_BIN`                                             | `composer` from `PATH`  | Default Composer binaries for all apps.                                                                                                     |
| `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED`, `RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE`                                     | `ON`, `file`            | Storage is `file`, `redis` (set `RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_*`) or `apcu`. The Docker images include the apcu extension but not redis.                |
| `RATE_LIMIT_API_MAX_REQUESTS`, `RATE_LIMIT_API_WINDOW_SECONDS`                 | `200`, `60`             | Requests per client IP on authenticated routes.                                                                                             |
| `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_FAILED_MAX_REQUESTS`, `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_FAILED_WINDOW_SECONDS` | `10`, `300`             | Failed logins per client IP. Once reached, the IP gets `429` on authenticated routes, even with valid credentials, until the window passes. |

Invalid values fail startup with `configuration_invalid`:

- `*_ENABLED`: `ON`/`OFF`, `TRUE`/`FALSE`, `YES`/`NO` or `1`/`0`, in any case.
- Numbers: whole numbers. Limits, windows and the clock skew window are at least `1`; the Redis port is `1`–`65535`.
- `RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE`: `redis` and `apcu` need their PHP extension when rate limiting is on.
- `MONOLOG_LEVEL`: `debug`, `info`, `notice`, `warning`, `error`, `critical`, `alert` or `emergency`.

## `config/apps.json`

- Use lowercase app ids.
- The dashboard treats app ids as global across all nodes. Make them unique by adding a server suffix, e.g. `shop-eu` and `shop-us`.
- Relative paths resolve against the **parent directory of the node repo**, not `config/`. With the node at `/srv/mata-node`, `example-app/logs/error.log` is `/srv/example-app/logs/error.log`. `logs`, `readme`, `composer.*` and `sessions.path` also take absolute paths.

Minimal example:

```
{
  "minimal-app": {
    "title": "Minimal Application",
    "url": "https://example.com/minimal",
    "path": "minimal-app",
    "env": "test",
    "logs": ["minimal-app/logs/error.log"]
  }
}
```

Full example:

```
{
  "example-app": {
    "title": "Example Application",
    "url": "https://example.com/app",
    "path": "example-app",
    "env": "prod",
    "description": "Example app",
    "disabled": false,
    "framework": "laravel",
    "status_endpoint": "https://example.com/app/health/",
    "monitoring": {
      "loganalysis": true,
      "logsize": true,
      "sessions": true,
      "reachability": true,
      "alarms": true,
      "events": true,
      "libraryaudit": true
    },
    "sessions": {
      "type": "file",
      "path": "example-app/temp/sessions",
      "filename_regex": "/^sess_/"
    },
    "logs": [
      {"type": "php_error_log", "paths": ["example-app/logs/error.log"]},
      {"type": "monolog", "paths": ["example-app/logs/app.log", "example-app/logs/debug.log"]},
      {"type": "json", "paths": ["example-app/logs/structured.log"]}
    ],
    "composer": {
      "json": "example-app/composer.json",
      "lock": "example-app/composer.lock",
      "bin": "example-app/composer.phar"
    }
  }
}
```

### App fields

| Key               | Required                                     | Default            | Purpose                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`           | for `/apps`                                  | –                  | Display name.                                                                                                                    |
| `url`             | for `/apps`                                  | –                  | Public URL.                                                                                                                      |
| `path`            | for `/apps`, `/readme`, Composer auto-detect | –                  | App base path.                                                                                                                   |
| `env`             | for `/apps`                                  | –                  | Exactly `dev`, `test`, `stg` or `prod`.                                                                                          |
| `logs`            | for a clean `/apps`                          | `[]`               | See [Logs](#logs).                                                                                                               |
| `description`     | No                                           | `""`               | Returned by `/apps`.                                                                                                             |
| `disabled`        | No                                           | `false`            | `true` (or `"true"`) hides the app and its routes.                                                                               |
| `status_endpoint` | No                                           | –                  | Absolute `http`/`https` URL; see below.                                                                                          |
| `readme`          | No                                           | `<path>/README.md` | Served by `/{app}/readme`.                                                                                                       |
| `monitoring`      | No                                           | all on             | See [Monitoring](#monitoring).                                                                                                   |
| `sessions`        | No                                           | unconfigured       | See [Sessions](#sessions).                                                                                                       |
| `framework`       | No                                           | detected           | Framework or CMS reported by `/apps`: a known identifier, any other name, or `none` to report none. See [Framework](#framework). |
| `composer`        | No                                           | off                | See [Composer](#composer).                                                                                                       |

**Status endpoint.** The dashboard sends an unauthenticated `GET` to `status_endpoint` and expects `{"maintenance_mode": false}` (or `true`). `/apps` returns it as `status_url`, or `null` when unset. Without it, the dashboard probes `url` instead and cannot detect maintenance mode.

### Monitoring

`monitoring` has seven switches, all `true` by default. List only the ones you turn off:

```
"monitoring": {"loganalysis": false, "sessions": false}
```

| Setting        | Applies to | When `false`                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `loganalysis`  | node       | No log parsing. `/apps` omits `status`; `/{app}/logs` returns `409`.                                     |
| `logsize`      | node       | No log globbing or sizing. `/apps` omits `logs`; `/{app}/logs-status` returns `409`.                     |
| `sessions`     | node       | No session directory scan or Redis `SCAN`. `/apps` omits `session`; `/{app}/sessions` returns `409`.     |
| `reachability` | dashboard  | Stops probing the app.                                                                                   |
| `alarms`       | dashboard  | Records events but never raises alarms.                                                                  |
| `events`       | dashboard  | Produces no events for the app.                                                                          |
| `libraryaudit` | dashboard  | Stops its scheduled Composer audit and library security events. `/{app}/composer-audit` stays available. |

A `409` body names the setting:

```
{"error": "Monitoring disabled", "message": "Monitoring disabled", "details": {"app": "archived-shop", "setting": "logsize"}}
```

`/{app}/readme`, `/{app}/libraries` and `/{app}/composer-audit` are never blocked.

**Validation.** Values must be JSON `true` or `false`. Anything else (`"off"`, `0`, `null`, …), unknown keys and a non-object `monitoring` make the app config invalid. Unknown keys are rejected so a typo like `"logsizes": false` cannot silently leave a scan running. An invalid config makes `/apps` and the app's blockable routes return `500` with the generic configuration error. Only the field name (`monitoring.<key>`) and app id are logged, never the value.

### Logs

`logs` is either a list of paths, with the parser auto-detected per file:

```
"logs": ["minimal-app/logs/error.log", "minimal-app/logs/app.log"]
```

or a list of groups:

```
"logs": [
  {"type": "monolog", "paths": ["example-app/logs/app.log"]},
  {"paths": ["example-app/logs/auto-detect.log"]}
]
```

| Key     | Required | Default     | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `paths` | Yes      | –           | Log file paths. Groups without paths are skipped.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `type`  | No       | auto-detect | `php_error_log`, `monolog`, `json`, a format in `resources/log-formats/` (e.g. `nginx_error`) or one in `config/log-formats/`. See [Log formats](https://docs.mata.sh/node/log-parsers/index.md). |

- **Auto-detection** samples a file's first 10 lines and picks the parser that matches at least half of them, falling back to `php_error_log`. An unknown `type` logs a warning and auto-detects. YAML-defined formats are never auto-detected.
- **Directories:** `/apps` log sizes and `/{app}/logs-status` include the `*.log` files inside a configured directory; `/{app}/logs` skips directories.
- **Memory:** for `/apps`, each file is streamed once, holding at most one line in memory (up to 5 MB; longer lines are streamed through).
- To see which parser a log gets and what it parses, run `make mata ARGS="log test <app>"`.

### Sessions

`sessions.type` is `file` (the default when `path` is set), `redis` or `none`. File example: see [the full example](#configappsjson). Redis example:

```
"sessions": {
  "type": "redis",
  "dsn": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0",
  "prefix": "PHPREDIS_SESSION:",
  "count_key": "mata:sessions:example-app:count",
  "scan_count": 1000,
  "timeout_seconds": 1.0,
  "cache_ttl_seconds": 60
}
```

| Key                 | Backend | Default             | Purpose                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`              | file    | empty               | Directory to scan. Missing, empty or not a directory gives counts of `0`.     |
| `filename_regex`    | file    | all files           | `preg_match()` pattern with delimiters, e.g. `"/^sess_/"`.                    |
| `dsn`               | redis   | –                   | Redis DSN. Required unless `dsn_env` is set.                                  |
| `dsn_env`           | redis   | –                   | Environment variable holding the DSN. Prefer it when the DSN has credentials. |
| `prefix`            | redis   | `PHPREDIS_SESSION:` | Session key prefix to scan for.                                               |
| `count_key`         | redis   | empty               | Key holding the session count; see below.                                     |
| `scan_count`        | redis   | `1000`              | `SCAN` `COUNT` hint.                                                          |
| `timeout_seconds`   | redis   | client default      | Socket timeout.                                                               |
| `cache_ttl_seconds` | redis   | `60`                | How long `SCAN` results are cached; `0` disables.                             |

**Counting Redis sessions.** Set `count_key` for large session stores: the node reads it with one `GET` and never scans. The node never writes the key; your app must keep it a non-negative integer. A missing key counts as `0`; a non-numeric value returns error metadata.

Without `count_key`, the node counts keys with `SCAN MATCH <prefix>*`. The count is approximate (`SCAN` can return duplicates), so use it for monitoring, not exact accounting. Results are cached in the node cache directory; the cache key contains no passwords or DSN credentials.

Redis reports only `count_total`; `count_last_hour`, `count_last_day`, `path` and `size_kb` are `null`.

### Composer

Used by `/apps/libraries`, `/apps/composer-audit` and `/{app}/libraries`.

`"composer": true` (or `"true"`, `"on"`, `"1"`, `"yes"`) reads `<path>/composer.json` and `<path>/composer.lock`. An object overrides individual settings:

```
"composer": {
  "json": "example-app/composer.json",
  "lock": "example-app/composer.lock",
  "bin": "example-app/composer.phar"
}
```

| Key       | Default                                     | Purpose                            |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `enabled` | `true` if any other key is set              | Truthy enables, falsy disables.    |
| `json`    | `<path>/composer.json`                      | Required for audits.               |
| `lock`    | `<path>/composer.lock`                      | Required for libraries and audits. |
| `bin`     | `COMPOSER_BIN`, else `composer` from `PATH` | A `.phar` is run as `php <bin>`.   |
| `php_bin` | `COMPOSER_PHP_BIN`, else `php`              | PHP binary for running a `.phar`.  |

### Framework

`/apps` reports `framework` as `{"name": "laravel", "version": "11.34.2"}` when a framework is declared or detected.

| `framework` config                    | Result                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| absent, `null` or blank               | Detect it from Composer packages and version files; omit `framework` if nothing matches. |
| `"none"`                              | Omit `framework`, without detection.                                                     |
| known identifier, such as `"laravel"` | Report that name, with the version read from its own files only, or `null`.              |
| any other string                      | Report it as `name` with `version: null`, without detection.                             |
| anything else                         | Log a warning and omit `framework`.                                                      |

Values are trimmed and case-sensitive: `"Laravel"` is reported as a custom name without a version. [Framework detection](https://docs.mata.sh/node/frameworks/index.md) lists the known identifiers and the files they are read from.

### App metadata responses

`/apps` returns, per app, these keys in this order:

```
"example-app": {
  "path": "example-app",
  "title": "Example Application",
  "url": "https://example.com/app",
  "env": "prod",
  "status_url": "https://example.com/app/health/",
  "description": "Example app",
  "composer": true,
  "framework": { "name": "laravel", "version": "11.34.2" },
  "status": { "fatal": 7, "warnings": 12, "total": 4231, "fatal_cursor": "v1:98cc…9ab" },
  "session": { "type": "file", "status": "ok", "count_last_hour": 1, "count_last_day": 2, "count_total": 2, "path": "example-app/temp/sessions", "size_kb": 12.34 },
  "logs": { "example-app/logs/error.log": 128.5 }
}
```

- `framework` is present only when a framework was declared or detected; `version` may be `null`. Consumers must accept custom and future `name` values.
- `status`, `logs` and `session` are present only when `loganalysis`, `logsize` and `sessions` are on. A missing key means "not measured", not zero or clean.
- `monitoring` is present only when a switch is off, and lists only those switches (all `false`) in the order of the [Monitoring](#monitoring) table, e.g. `"monitoring": {"loganalysis": false, "sessions": false}`.
- `/{app}/sessions` returns the same `session` object.

**`status`.** `fatal`, `warnings` and `total` are summed over all the app's logs. `fatal_cursor` is `null` when `fatal` is `0`, otherwise `v1:` plus 64 lowercase hex characters.

The cursor is an opaque fingerprint of the app's fatal entries, meant only for comparison: if it differs from the last value, the fatal entries changed. It contains no log content, paths, file identity, offsets or per-entry hashes; entries are in `/{app}/logs` and file details in `/{app}/logs-status`.

- **Changes when** a fatal entry is added (even a duplicate), when a fatal entry's timestamp, message, stack trace, context, repeat count or order changes, or when log rotation replaces a file containing fatal entries. Multiline stack traces count; JSON records are canonicalized first, so key order does not matter.
- **Stays the same when** warnings, notices, info or other lines are appended, and across node restarts. The node is stateless, so rewriting a file with exactly the same fatal entries in the same positions looks unchanged.

## `config/databases.json`

Named connections to MariaDB, MySQL or PostgreSQL servers, used by the `/databases/*` routes. `{}` turns database monitoring off; the routes then return `404`.

```
{
  "connections": {
    "shop": {
      "engine": "mariadb",
      "connection": {
        "host": "localhost",
        "port": "3306",
        "username": "mata_monitor",
        "password": "secret"
      },
      "databases": {
        "app_db": "Main application",
        "analytics_db": "Reporting"
      }
    },
    "reporting": {
      "engine": "pgsql",
      "connection": {
        "host": "10.0.0.5",
        "port": 5432,
        "username": "mata_monitor",
        "password": "secret"
      },
      "databases": {
        "warehouse": "Data warehouse"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

| Field         | Meaning                                                                             |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `connections` | Name => connection; at least one.                                                   |
| `engine`      | `mariadb` (also for MySQL) or `pgsql`.                                              |
| `connection`  | `host`, `port` (string or number), `username`, `password`. Use a read-only account. |
| `databases`   | Database name => description shown in the dashboard; at least one.                  |

- All fields are required. Unknown keys or missing fields fail startup with `configuration_invalid`. Startup never connects, so a database outage cannot stop the node.
- The connection name appears in the dashboard, the API and dashboard URLs. It may contain only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.
- Use one connection per login. The same database may appear under several connections.

**Responses.** `/databases/overview` returns one entry per connection with `connection`, `engine`, `collected_at`, the server-wide `status` (connections, limits, uptime), `databases` and `error`. A failing connection has `status: null` and `error: {"status_code": 503, ...}` and its reason is logged as a warning; the other connections are still reported. `/databases/processes?connection=NAME` lists only sessions on that connection's databases.

**Privileges.** The account needs no write rights. Without the privileges below, `/databases/processes` reports `"visibility": "own_sessions"` and shows only the account's own sessions.

- MariaDB/MySQL: `GRANT PROCESS ON *.* TO 'mata_monitor'@'...'`. `PROCESS` granted only through a role also counts as `own_sessions`.
- PostgreSQL: `GRANT pg_read_all_stats TO mata_monitor`, or superuser. Without it, the overview's `connections` and `running` also count only the account's own sessions. The node connects to the `postgres` database. `max_used_connections`, `refused_connections` and `aborted_connects` have no PostgreSQL equivalent and are `null`.

## `config/transmit.json`

One object; every key is optional.

```
{
  "check_disk_space_enabled": "on",
  "check_disk_space_path": "/",
  "errorlog_readout_limit": 200,
  "errorlog_scan_line_limit": 20000,
  "system_filecount_cache_max_age": 1800,
  "cronjob_heartbeats": ["logs/cron/heartbeat-daily.log"],
  "cronjob_heartbeat_stale_seconds": 86400,
  "cronjob_heartbeat_tail_line_limit": 50
}
```

| Key                                 | Default | Purpose                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `check_disk_space_enabled`          | on      | Only the exact string `"off"` disables disk checks; anything else, even `false`, enables them.              |
| `check_disk_space_path`             | `/`     | Filesystem to check. Use an absolute path. Disk values are returned in KiB.                                 |
| `errorlog_readout_limit`            | `50`    | Entries returned per file by `/{app}/logs` after filtering and grouping; repeats of one message count once. |
| `errorlog_scan_line_limit`          | `20000` | Tail lines read per file before `/{app}/logs` parses and filters them.                                      |
| `system_filecount_cache_max_age`    | `1800`  | Seconds a cached server file count is reused.                                                               |
| `cronjob_heartbeats`                | `[]`    | Heartbeat file paths, relative to the node root. A single string also works.                                |
| `cronjob_heartbeat_stale_seconds`   | `86400` | Heartbeat files older than this are stale.                                                                  |
| `cronjob_heartbeat_tail_line_limit` | `50`    | Lines returned in `content_tail`.                                                                           |

The two `cronjob_heartbeat_*` numbers fall back to the default when not numeric and are at least `1`.

### Cron heartbeats

Cron runs per host, so heartbeats are configured per node, here rather than per app. `/server/data` returns a summary:

```
"cronjobs": {"total": 2, "working": 1, "stale": 0, "missing": 1}
```

`/server/cronjobs` returns one entry per file, in configured order:

```
[
  {
    "index": 0,
    "path": "logs/cron/heartbeat-daily.log",
    "exists": true,
    "mtime": "2026-07-07 12:00:00",
    "age_seconds": 42,
    "size": 1234,
    "stale": false,
    "content_tail": ["last line"]
  }
]
```

# Docker

MATA Node runs as a single `mata-web` container (PHP 8.3 + Apache) on port `3310`. It has no database container; databases listed in `config/databases.json` are reached over the network.

## Files

| File                             | Purpose                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.env`                           | Compose settings: `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, `WEB_PORT`, `PHP_VERSION`, `COMPOSER_VERSION`, `APP_ENV`                        |
| `docker-compose.yml`             | Base service, port mapping, env files, external `mata-network`                                                            |
| `docker-compose.dev.yml`         | `Dockerfile.dev`, source bind mount, `vendor` named volume                                                                |
| `docker-compose.prod.yml`        | Multi-stage `Dockerfile`, read-only `config/`, log rotation, `no-new-privileges`                                          |
| `docker/apache/000-default.conf` | Vhost: document root `public/`, security headers, denies `config/`, `src/`, `vendor/`, `logs/`, `temp/`                   |
| `docker/php/php-{dev,prod}.ini`  | PHP settings per environment                                                                                              |
| `docker/cron/crontab`            | `www-data` crontab, empty by default                                                                                      |
| `docker/entrypoint-dev.sh`       | Dev only: maps `www-data` to the host UID/GID, creates `temp/` and `logs/`, runs `composer install` if `vendor/` is empty |

The app itself is configured in `config/`; see the [configuration reference](https://docs.mata.sh/node/configuration/index.md).

## Development

```
make dev-start      # runs docker-setup on first start
curl http://localhost:3310/health
```

The `make` targets that start containers create the external `mata-network` (shared with MATA Dashboard) if it does not exist yet.

`make docker-setup` creates `.env` and the `config/` files from their examples and asks for `DASHBOARD_API_KEY`. Source changes apply immediately. Env file changes do not: run `make dev-recreate` (`make dev-restart` keeps the old environment).

## Production

```
cp .env.example .env
make bootstrap-config             # then edit config/
make prod-start
```

The image contains the code and production dependencies only. `config/` is mounted read-only; `logs/` and `temp/` are mounted writable. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy in front of the container.

## Monitoring the host from a container

The node reports what it can see from inside its container, which by default is less than a native install sees:

| Data                                                    | Seen by default                                       | To see the host                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| CPU, memory                                             | Host values (`/proc` is shared with the host)         | Nothing to do                                               |
| Disk                                                    | The container's filesystem at `check_disk_space_path` | Mount the host path and point `check_disk_space_path` at it |
| Process count, PHP processes                            | The container's own processes only                    | `pid: host`                                                 |
| Logs, sessions, README, Composer files, cron heartbeats | Nothing outside the node                              | Read-only bind mounts                                       |

App paths in `apps.json` resolve against the node's parent directory, which is `/var/www` in the image. Mount each app below it and keep the relative paths:

```
services:
  mata-web:
    pid: host
    volumes:
      - /srv/shop:/var/www/shop:ro    # apps.json: "path": "shop", "logs": ["shop/var/log/prod.log"]
      - /srv:/host/srv:ro             # transmit.json: "check_disk_space_path": "/host/srv"
```

- `make prod-start` names its Compose files explicitly, so a `docker-compose.override.yml` is not read. Add the lines to `docker-compose.prod.yml`.
- Mounted files must be readable by `www-data` (UID 33) inside the container. Check with `make shell-www`.
- `pid: host` shows the node every host process with its command line, as a native install sees them.

Applications that run in their own containers are visible only through files they write to the host. Point their log directory (`storage/logs`, `var/log`) at a host directory and mount that into the node. Output that goes only to stdout/stderr (`docker logs`), and Composer files baked into an image, are not visible to the node.

If the mounts get unwieldy, run the node natively on the host instead; it then reads everything its user can read.

## Commands

| Command                               | Action                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `make dev-start` / `dev-stop`         | Start / stop dev                                     |
| `make dev-recreate`                   | Recreate containers to reload env files              |
| `make dev-rebuild` / `prod-rebuild`   | Rebuild without cache                                |
| `make prod-start` / `prod-stop`       | Start / stop production                              |
| `make logs` / `logs-app` / `logs-php` | Container / app / PHP error logs                     |
| `make shell` / `shell-www`            | Shell as root / `www-data`                           |
| `make test`                           | PHPUnit in the running container                     |
| `make composer-rebuild`               | Drop the `vendor` volume and reinstall               |
| `make docker-clean`                   | Remove this project's containers, volumes and images |

## Troubleshooting

- **`network mata-network declared as external, but could not be found`**: you ran `docker-compose` directly; run `make docker-network` once, or use the `make` targets.
- **Port 3310 in use**: set `WEB_PORT` in `.env`.
- **`/health` returns 503 with `configuration_missing`**: run `make bootstrap-config`; all five files in `config/` must exist.
- **Config change not picked up**: `make dev-recreate`.

# Framework detection

`/apps` reports each app's framework or CMS as `{"name": "laravel", "version": "11.34.2"}`. How the `apps.json` `framework` key controls this is in the [configuration reference](https://docs.mata.sh/node/configuration/#framework); this page covers what automatic detection and version lookup read.

## Known identifiers and packages

The table is also the detection order: products precede the Laravel and Symfony frameworks they may depend on.

| Identifier    | Identifying Composer packages, in priority order                                                     |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shopware`    | `shopware/core`                                                                                      |
| `joomla`      | `joomla/joomla-cms`                                                                                  |
| `cakephp`     | `cakephp/cakephp`                                                                                    |
| `magento`     | `magento/product-enterprise-edition`, `magento/product-community-edition`                            |
| `sylius`      | `sylius/sylius`                                                                                      |
| `craft`       | `craftcms/cms`                                                                                       |
| `statamic`    | `statamic/cms`                                                                                       |
| `contao`      | `contao/core-bundle`                                                                                 |
| `sulu`        | `sulu/sulu`                                                                                          |
| `neos`        | `neos/neos`                                                                                          |
| `october`     | `october/rain`                                                                                       |
| `yii`         | `yiisoft/yii2`                                                                                       |
| `codeigniter` | `codeigniter4/framework`                                                                             |
| `laravel`     | `laravel/framework`                                                                                  |
| `drupal`      | `drupal/core`                                                                                        |
| `typo3`       | `typo3/cms-core`                                                                                     |
| `wordpress`   | `roots/wordpress-no-content`, `johnpbloch/wordpress-core`, `roots/wordpress`, `johnpbloch/wordpress` |
| `symfony`     | `symfony/framework-bundle`                                                                           |

A package matches in `vendor/composer/installed.json`, runtime `composer.lock` packages, or `composer.json`'s root `name`. Root projects such as Joomla and Sylius therefore need no package entry for themselves. Dev-only packages do not identify the framework. Requirement constraints in `composer.json` never supply identity or a deployed version.

## Source probes

The Composer root is the directory of the configured `composer.lock`, else configured `composer.json`, else `<path>/composer.json`. Detection honors `config.vendor-dir` and WordPress's `extra.wordpress-install-dir`, even when Composer auditing is disabled. Source probes check only these fixed paths, relative to the app and Composer roots unless shown under `vendor/`:

| Identifier  | Source probe                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `joomla`    | `administrator/manifests/files/joomla.xml`                                                                                                                                              |
| `laravel`   | `vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Foundation/Application.php`                                                                                                                    |
| `drupal`    | `core/lib/Drupal.php`, `web/core/lib/Drupal.php`, `docroot/core/lib/Drupal.php`                                                                                                         |
| `typo3`     | `vendor/typo3/cms-core/Classes/Information/Typo3Version.php`, `typo3/sysext/core/Classes/Information/Typo3Version.php`, `public/typo3/sysext/core/Classes/Information/Typo3Version.php` |
| `wordpress` | `wp-includes/version.php` in the roots, `wp/`, `wordpress/`, `web/wp/`, or the configured WordPress install directory                                                                   |
| `symfony`   | `vendor/symfony/http-kernel/Kernel.php`, for version only                                                                                                                               |

An existing source probe can identify its framework even when its version cannot be parsed. Symfony requires a package or root-name match because other products ship its components. The other identifiers use package/root identity only.

## Version precedence

Versions come from installed packages first, then the product's own source probe, then runtime lock packages. Package priority follows the table above. Symfony uses `symfony/http-kernel` for its version, not `symfony/framework-bundle`. October intentionally reports `version: null`: `october/rain` identifies the CMS but its library patch version is not the deployed CMS version.

Only concrete release versions are returned, with a leading `v` removed. Branches such as `dev-main` and `12.x-dev`, missing versions and unreadable files yield `null` if no other source provides a version. Unreadable or invalid detection files are logged and skipped; framework reporting never fails `/apps`. A known declaration still reports its name if detection files are unavailable.

## Cost and caching

The node never executes application code, `wp-cli`, `artisan` or `bin/console`, and never scans directories. Each `/apps` request reads `composer.json` and checks the files above; the rest is parsed again only when one of them changes, the declaration changes, or 24 hours pass.

# Log formats

The node parses `php_error_log`, `monolog` and `json` logs with built-in parsers, and every format defined in a YAML file. `type` in a log group of `apps.json` names the format:

```
"logs": [{ "type": "plain_level", "paths": ["shop/logs/app.log"] }]
```

Without `type`, the node auto-detects `json`, `monolog` or `php_error_log` per file and falls back to `php_error_log`. Formats defined in YAML are never auto-detected: they apply only where `type` names them.

## Defining a format

Put one file per format in `config/log-formats/`, named after the format: `plain_level.yaml` or `plain_level.yml` defines `plain_level`. Names use lowercase letters, digits and underscores. The directory is optional, and in Docker it is part of the read-only `config/` mount.

A format with a pattern, for a log like `2026-10-09T12:00:00Z ERROR Payment failed`:

```
# config/log-formats/plain_level.yaml
description: Plain lines with a level
pattern: '^(?<timestamp>\S+Z) (?<level>[A-Z]+) (?<message>.*)$'
levels:
  error: [ERROR, FATAL]
  warning: [WARN]
```

A format for one JSON record per line, such as `{"@timestamp": "…", "log.level": "error", "message": "…"}`:

```
json:
  timestamp: '@timestamp'
  level: log.level
  message: message
levels:
  error: [error, critical]
  warning: [warning]
```

| Key           | Required            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pattern`     | `pattern` or `json` | Regular expression (PCRE) for the first line of an entry, without delimiters. Named groups `level` and `message` are required, `timestamp` is optional, and any other named group is passed through as a key of the entry. Write it in single quotes so backslashes stay as written; `(?i)` at the start makes it case-insensitive. |
| `json`        | `pattern` or `json` | Fields of the record for `level`, `message` and, optionally, `timestamp`. A field is a key as written, else a dotted path into nested objects: `log.level` finds `{"log.level": …}` and `{"log": {"level": …}}`.                                                                                                                    |
| `levels`      | Yes                 | The levels that are an `error` and those that are a `warning`. Compared without case; every other level is `Other`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `description` | No                  | Free text for people reading the file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

How the node reads a format:

- **Entries:** with a pattern, a line it matches starts an entry, and the lines up to the next match belong to its message, such as a stack trace. A JSON format reads each line as one entry and skips lines that are no JSON record.
- **Type and counts:** the level gives the entry's `type` (`Error`, `Warning` or `Other`), which `/{app}/logs` filters on, and the `fatal` and `warnings` counts of `/apps`. Those count entries whose first line has an error or warning level.
- **Timestamps:** most notations are read, such as `2026-10-26 08:00:00`, `2026/10/26 08:00:00`, ISO 8601 and `26/Oct/2026:08:00:00 +0000`, and returned as `Y-m-d H:i:s`. A timestamp the node cannot read is returned as `""`.
- **Limits:** a pattern sees only the first 8 KiB of a line, and a match that needs more than 100,000 backtracking steps counts as no match, so a crafted log line cannot make the node slow.

`make mata ARGS="config validate"` reports a broken format file as a warning; the node does not log it. The node skips that format: apps naming it get an auto-detected parser, as for any unknown `type`. Check the result on real logs with `make mata ARGS="log test shop"`. It shows the parser each file gets, the entries it parses, and the fatal and warning counts (see [Command line](https://docs.mata.sh/node/cli/index.md)).

A format file belongs to the instance, like `apps.json`: version it together with the rest of `config/`. The node's `.gitignore` excludes `config/log-formats/`, so updating a checkout never touches it.

## Grouping

`/{app}/logs` groups the parsed entries before applying the readout limit: entries of the same `type` whose messages differ only in timestamps, IDs and numbers become one entry, the newest, with `count`, `first_seen` and `last_seen`. A source location such as `Db.php:75` or `line 75` is not masked, so the same message from another line stays separate. Counts and `first_seen` cover only the scanned lines (`errorlog_scan_line_limit`), not the whole file.

```
{"grouped": true, "readout_limit": 200, "entries": {"logs/error.log": [
  {"timestamp": "2026-10-25 22:48:49", "type": "Error", "message": "MySQL server has gone away in /src/Db.php:75",
   "count": 42, "first_seen": "2026-10-25 08:01:12", "last_seen": "2026-10-25 22:48:49"}]}}
```

## Adding a format to the node

A format that other installations than yours use too belongs in the node itself. Open a pull request with:

- the format file in `resources/log-formats/`, written as for `config/log-formats/` (see `nginx_error.yaml`);
- a log fixture in `src/Tests/Fixtures/logs/`, with a test that parses it (see `DefinedLogParserTest`).

Shipped formats take their names first: a file in `config/log-formats/` with the same name is skipped, so a name means the same format on every node.

The built-in parsers in `src/Watchers/LogParsers/` are PHP because they need more than a pattern, such as auto-detection.

# Shell command surface

Policy: keep shell commands for performant OS/log work, but build command strings only in `src/Services/Command/ShellCommands.php`.

| Builder                                 | Command shape                          | Inputs                                  | Risk                     | Decision                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ShellCommands::tail()`                 | `tail -n N -- FILE`                    | file path, line count                   | path/arg injection       | Keep shell. Centralized escaping and line clamp.                     |
| `ShellCommands::lineCount()`            | `wc -l < FILE`                         | file path                               | path injection           | Keep shell for large logs. Centralized escaping.                     |
| `ShellCommands::composerAudit()`        | `composer audit ... --working-dir=DIR` | optional composer bin path, working dir | config path injection    | Keep shell. Bin/path escaped; default command is literal `composer`. |
| `ShellCommands::processCount()`         | `pgrep -c[x] PATTERN 2>/dev/null`      | process regex                           | regex/shell injection    | Keep shell. Pattern character allowlist plus escaping.               |
| `ShellCommands::memoryTotalKb()`        | \`grep MemTotal /proc/meminfo          | awk '{print $2}'\`                      | none                     | low                                                                  |
